_status: DRAFT for owner review (Nov 2026). Written only from data/trade-paths.json (key points, lessons, sign-offs, path notes) and the Oct 2026 sales sessions. Every module now has 5 questions; every module with a role-play persona has steps.

questions.q: A customer says a competitor quoted cheaper. What does Proximity compete on?
options: Price: we match the cheaper quote
Trust and quality, with a fixed upfront price
questions.why: We never compete on price. Competitors like Mr Emergency compete on price and speed; we compete on trust and quality.

questions.q: On a $1,000 job, roughly how much is profit?
questions.why: Roughly 50% labour and materials, 30% running the business, 20% profit: about $200 on a $1,000 job.

questions.q: You give a 10% discount on a $1,000 job. What happens to the profit?
options: It drops by about half: $100 of the $200
It goes up because we win the job
questions.why: A $100 discount comes straight out of the roughly $200 profit, so half of it is gone.

questions.q: The customer has a fixed upfront price. Who pays for hours you didn't estimate?
options: The customer, on the next invoice
The office absorbs it at month end
We do: they come out of our profit
questions.why: With a fixed upfront price, unestimated hours and unbilled materials come out of our profit, not the customer's pocket.

questions.q: What is Proximity's reputation built on?
options: Our 4.9★ reviews: every visit adds to them or damages them
questions.why: Our reputation is the 4.9★ review base, and every single visit adds to it or damages it.

questions.q: Something on site feels unsafe, but you're not sure. What do you do?
options: Stop and ask. Nobody is criticised for stopping a job
Ask the customer what they think
questions.why: Anyone can stop a job if it's unsafe, and nobody is ever criticised for it. If you're unsure, stop and ask.

questions.q: Before you work on water or gas, you…
options: Isolate and test, every time, no exceptions
Ask the customer to turn it off
questions.why: Isolate and test water and gas before starting. No exceptions.

questions.q: You need to cut into a wall and suspect asbestos. What now?
options: Wet it down and cut carefully
Wear a mask and cut quickly
Ask the customer whether it's asbestos
Stop, photograph it, flag it in ServiceTitan and call the Install Manager or the office
questions.why: Never cut, drill or break suspected asbestos. Stop, photograph, flag it in ServiceTitan, and call the Install Manager (Charlotte, interim) or the office.

questions.q: Compliance paperwork and certificates are…
options: Office admin done at month end
Part of the job, and lodged on time
questions.why: Compliance paperwork is part of the job, not admin afterwards. Certificates are lodged on time.

questions.q: An apprentice is on your job. Which is right?
options: They can do anything they feel confident with
They work alone on small jobs
They only do work their licence covers, with a named supervisor on every job
They only need supervising on Saturdays
questions.why: Only do work your licence covers. Supervised workers have a named supervisor on every job.

questions.q: You did extra work but didn't record it in ServiceTitan. As far as the business is concerned…
options: It happened, because the customer saw it
The office will work it out
It's fine as long as you remember
questions.why: If it isn't in ServiceTitan, it didn't happen: notes, photos, videos, time, payment and sign-off.

questions.q: When do you update statuses, forms and timesheets?
options: At the end of the week
At the end of each day
As you go: tools out, timer on
questions.why: Statuses, forms and timesheets are updated as you go, never at the end of the week.

questions.q: What do you check before you knock on the door?
options: The customer's and the equipment's history in ServiceTitan
questions.why: Always check customer and equipment history before you knock. Past jobs and recommendations matter.

questions.q: Where does every price come from?
options: The pricebook or an approved template
questions.why: Every price comes from the pricebook or an approved template. No hand-typed prices.

questions.q: Which of these must be recorded in ServiceTitan?
options: Notes, photos, videos, time, payment and sign-off
questions.why: All of it: notes, photos, videos, time, payment and sign-off.

questions.q: What sets the tone for the whole visit?
options: The first 30 seconds: on time (or call ahead), professional, protecting their home
questions.why: The first 30 seconds set the tone. Be on time or call ahead, look professional, and protect their home.

questions.q: A customer complains the last tech was late. What do you say?
options: "I'm sorry about that. Let's get this sorted for you today."
questions.why: Customers judge the whole company by you. Never blame dispatch, the office or another tech.

questions.q: A customer demands money off while you're on site. You…
options: Explain why the price is fair until they agree
Stay calm and listen, promise no refund or discount, then call the Install Manager or the office and log it
questions.why: Stay calm, listen, and never promise a refund or discount. Log it so the Customer Service team takes over the complaint.

questions.q: On a tenant job, who approves the work?
options: The property manager. The tenant gives access
questions.why: Tenant jobs: the property manager approves, and the tenant gives access.

questions.q: On a strata job, what extra thing must you record?
options: Whether it's common property or a lot
questions.why: Strata: record common property vs lot. It changes who approves and who pays.

sim.scenario: The job is taking longer than expected and the customer wants money off.

steps.them: This was meant to take two hours. It's been four. I want money off.
options: "I understand, that's frustrating. Can you tell me what's worrying you most?"
"It's not my fault. Dispatch booked it wrong."
"Prices are fixed. Nothing I can do."
steps.feedback: Stay calm and listen first. No discounts, and no blaming anyone.

steps.them: So are you taking something off or not?
options: "I can't promise a refund or discount, but I'll get this logged now and the team will call you."
"Maybe, if you leave us a 5-star review."
steps.feedback: Never promise a refund or discount on site. Hand it to the people who can resolve it.

steps.them: Fine. Who's going to call me?
options: "I'm calling the Install Manager or the office right now to log it. Our Customer Service team will take it from there."
"Leave a review and they'll see it."
steps.feedback: Log it and hand it over, so the Customer Service team owns the complaint.

questions.q: Which jobs need before-and-after photos and video?
questions.why: Every job gets before-and-after photos and video. They protect you, prove the work and feed the reports.

questions.q: Which job note is best?
options: "Photo 3: corroded flexi hose under the kitchen sink. Recommend replacing all flexis."
questions.why: Number your photos and refer to them in your notes, with what you found and what you recommend.

questions.q: Which wording belongs in customer-facing notes?
options: "Showing signs of age and worth a licensed assessment"
questions.why: Record observations, not legal opinions. Never write 'illegal' or 'non-compliant' in customer-facing notes.

questions.q: You find something the customer must deal with today. You…
options: Mention it at the next visit
Put it at the bottom of the invoice
Flag it as urgent so the office calls the same day
Leave it, it's not your job
questions.why: Flag anything urgent so the office calls the same day.

questions.q: Why do photos and video matter?
options: They protect you, prove the work and feed the reports
They don't, they slow you down
questions.why: They protect you, prove the work and become the reports that win the next job.

questions.q: When are payment and customer sign-off collected?
options: Before you leave, in ServiceTitan. No exceptions without office approval
At the end of the month
questions.why: Payment and sign-off are collected in ServiceTitan before you leave.

questions.q: On installs, who owns payment collection?
options: The Install Manager (Charlotte, interim). The installer collects the balance on site
questions.why: The Install Manager owns payment collection and the customer's happiness. The installer collects the balance on site, and anything overdue goes to Chloe.

questions.q: How is planned work paid for?
options: 50% upfront when approved, the balance on completion
questions.why: Planned work is 50% upfront when approved, with the balance on completion.

questions.q: A job for a property manager, strata or builder account is paid…
questions.why: Accounts customers follow their account terms.

questions.q: What does a genuine 5-star review earn you?
options: $100, and it brings in the next customer
questions.why: Every genuine 5-star review earns you $100 and brings in the next customer.

sim.scenario: The homeowner is happy with the work but wants to be invoiced and pay next week.

steps.them: Great job! Just invoice me and I'll pay next week.
options: "Glad you're happy! Our policy is payment on completion, so I can take it now. What's easiest for you?"
"Pay now or I take the parts back."
"Pay cash and I'll do you a deal."
steps.feedback: Stay friendly, restate the policy, and offer the payment options.

steps.them: I really can't today. Payday's Friday.
options: "No problem. Let me call the office now so we sort it properly before I go."
"Then I'm taking the new tap back out."
steps.feedback: Escalate to the office rather than leaving the job unpaid.

questions.q: Why does a bad scope matter?
options: It doesn't, install sorts it out
It costs the installer time and the business its profit
questions.why: Each role depends on the one before it. A bad scope costs the installer time and the business its profit.

questions.q: You hit a parts or access problem on an install. Who do you call first?
questions.why: Raise issues with the Install Manager (Charlotte, interim) straight away: scope, parts, access, customer.

questions.q: You spot extra work the customer needs. How do you raise it?
options: Mention it to the office when you're back
Tell the customer to ring later
In ServiceTitan, with photos and notes
questions.why: Extra work is raised in ServiceTitan with photos and notes, never just a verbal 'mention it to the office'.

questions.q: Lots of warranty and same-day-return jobs usually means…
questions.why: Warranty and same-day-return jobs are handled graciously, but a lot of them signals a quality problem.

questions.q: Who can approve a change to a price?
questions.why: Only Harriet (Sales Manager) or Sadie (Office Manager) can change a price. Techs never can.

questions.q: Which two numbers does Dispatch Pro rank you on?
questions.why: Average ticket and close rate are the only two numbers the Sales Manager watches, and the two Dispatch Pro ranks you on.

questions.q: From $213K a month, +$250 on the ticket and +5 points of close rate gets you to about…
questions.why: Small lifts multiply: +$250 ticket and +5 points of close rate takes $213K to about $248K a month, with no extra days.

questions.q: When do Saturdays count in Dispatch Pro?
options: Only when they're rostered as regular shifts
questions.why: Dispatch Pro only assigns techs on regular shifts. Saturdays must be rostered as regular shifts to count.

questions.q: 10 jobs at $2,000 vs 11 jobs at $2,200. What's the lift?
options: About +21%, because the two numbers multiply
questions.why: $20,000 becomes $24,200. A 10% bigger ticket and one extra yes multiply to +21%.

questions.q: How is Sales Tech commission earned?
questions.why: Commission is 5% of sales paid in full.

questions.q: After a complete handover, who does the job belong to?
questions.why: Sales Techs only sell. After a complete handover, the job belongs to the Install Manager.

questions.q: What's the test of a finished handover?
options: You uploaded at least one photo
Could the installer do the job without ever calling you?
questions.why: If the installer would need to call you, the handover isn't finished.

questions.q: Who collects the 50% deposit, and when?
options: The Install Manager on install day
questions.why: You collect the 50% deposit at signing. No deposit, no booking, no materials ordered.

questions.q: Who collects the balance?
options: The customer pays whenever they like
questions.why: The Install Manager collects the balance on completion.

questions.q: Why does a clean handover protect your pay?
options: Commission is paid on sales paid in full
questions.why: Commission is paid on sales paid in full, so a job that stalls or comes back hurts you too.

sim.scenario: Last lead of a long day. The customer has just signed a $16K Elite bathroom job.

steps.them: It's 6:40pm. What goes in the scope?
options: "See photos." The installer will work it out
The scope, in and out, line by line from the pricebook
steps.feedback: Finish the scope properly. 'See photos' is how installers end up calling you.

steps.them: The customer asks: "So who do I talk to now?"
options: "Call me any time, day or night."
"The Install Manager will call you next to book everything in."
"Just ring the main number and see."
steps.feedback: Set the customer up: the Install Manager calls them next.

steps.them: Before you leave the driveway…
options: Record access, specials and the customer's expectations, and confirm the 50% deposit is collected
Head home and finish it tomorrow
Nothing, it's all in the system
steps.feedback: Access, specials, expectations and the deposit, done before you leave.

questions.q: What comes first on any quote?
questions.why: Diagnose first and price last.

questions.q: Why does every estimate say what's included and what isn't?
options: It protects the fixed-price, no-hidden-costs promise
It makes the quote look longer
questions.why: Clear inclusions and exclusions protect the fixed-price, no-hidden-costs promise.

questions.q: Why do realistic hours matter on an estimate?
options: They don't, because the customer pays a fixed price
The installer's time and the business's profit depend on them
questions.why: Realistic hours matter because the installer's time and the business's profit depend on them.

questions.q: Which option do you present first?
questions.why: Elite is the best outcome, future-proofed, and is presented first.

questions.q: The customer called about a tap, but you also find perished flexi hoses. Your quote…
options: Bundles the related items into Standard, Premium and Elite
Leaves the hoses for next time
questions.why: Never quote one job when the site shows more. Standard, Premium and Elite bundle the related items you found.

questions.q: Why use estimate templates?
options: Every customer gets the same price and wording for the same job
They let you set your own price
questions.why: Templates mean every customer gets the same price and wording for the same job.

questions.q: A template already exists for the job. You…
options: Build from scratch so it's tailored
questions.why: Never build from scratch when a template exists.

questions.q: When should a new template be created?
questions.why: New templates are for job types quoted repeatedly.

questions.q: Before a new template goes live, it must be…
questions.why: New templates are reviewed and signed off before going live.

questions.q: What does a good template include?
options: Standard scope wording, inclusions, exclusions, materials and estimated hours
questions.why: A template carries standard scope wording, inclusions, exclusions, materials and estimated hours.

questions.q: On a $1,000 job, roughly how much is profit?
questions.why: About 50% labour and materials, 30% running the business, 20% profit: about $200 on a $1,000 job.

questions.q: What does a 10% discount on a $1,000 job do?
options: Takes $100, which is half of the $200 profit
Pays for itself by winning more work
questions.why: A 10% discount takes $100 off the $1,000 job, which is half the $200 profit.

questions.q: Who pays for an hour you didn't estimate?
options: It comes straight out of the profit
questions.why: Every unestimated hour comes straight out of the profit.

questions.q: Who can change a price?
questions.why: Techs can't discount or change a price. Only Harriet (Sales Manager) or Sadie (Office Manager) can.

questions.q: A customer asks for a better price. What do you say?
options: "Let me ask the office for a better price."
"I can't change the price, but I can show you a lower option."
"Pay cash and we'll sort something out."
questions.why: Never offer to 'ask the office for a better price' in front of a customer: that's a discount by another name. Step down an option instead.

questions.q: What's the order for presenting a proposal?
options: Problem → fix → options → the Proximity promise → let them choose
questions.why: Problem → fix → options → the Proximity promise → let them choose.

questions.q: Why use the customer's own photos and video?
questions.why: Use their photos and video. Showing beats telling.

questions.q: A modest house and a worried-looking owner. What do you present?
options: Whatever you think they can afford
questions.why: Never prejudge what someone can afford. Present every option at every door, Elite first.

questions.q: You've just said the price. Now you…
options: Stay quiet and let the customer speak first
questions.why: Scope. Price. Silence. Never discount to fill the quiet.

questions.q: The customer isn't ready to decide. You…
options: Agree when you'll follow up, and log it in ServiceTitan
questions.why: If they're not ready, that's fine. Agree when you'll follow up and log it in ServiceTitan.

sim.scenario: The hot water unit is failing. The customer balks at the price and wants to 'think about it'.

steps.them: That's a lot more than I expected. The Elite one especially.
options: "Totally fair. Is it the overall cost that worries you, or whether it's worth it?"
steps.feedback: Ask whether the concern is the price or the value. No flinch and no discount.

steps.them: Remind me what I actually get with you?
options: "A fixed upfront price, no hidden costs, a lifetime labour warranty and same-day return."
steps.feedback: Clarify the options and the promise. That's what they're paying for.

steps.them: I think I need to think about it.
options: "If you sign today I'll do you a deal."
"No worries. When's a good time for me to follow up, Thursday or Friday?"
steps.feedback: 'Not yet' is fine. Agree the follow-up time and log it. No discounts and no fake urgency.

questions.q: No 50% deposit means…
options: No scheduling and no materials ordered
questions.why: No 50% deposit, no scheduling and no materials ordered.

questions.q: When is the balance paid?
questions.why: 50% upfront when the plan is approved, and the balance on completion.

questions.q: Why does the handover matter so much?
options: It's your promise to the installer and the customer: missing information costs everyone time
It doesn't, install sorts it out
questions.why: The handover is your promise to the installer and the customer. Missing information costs everyone time.

questions.q: What goes in the handover?
options: Scope, materials, photos, access, hours and customer notes
questions.why: The handover carries the scope, materials, photos, access, hours and customer notes.

questions.q: Who accepts install handovers?
questions.why: Handovers are accepted by residential dispatch (Kim) when nothing is missing.

questions.q: What drives Install Tech pay?
options: The gap between estimated and actual hours
questions.why: Your pay is driven by the gap between estimated and actual hours.

questions.q: Roughly how much value is created for each hour saved against the estimate?
questions.why: Every hour saved against the estimate is worth about $50.

questions.q: What does a warranty return do?
options: Wipes out the time you saved and costs the business its profit on the job
questions.why: A warranty return wipes out the time you saved and costs the business its profit on the job.

questions.q: Speed without quality is…
options: Failure, because the lifetime labour warranty brings the job back
Fine if the customer is happy today
Only a problem on big jobs
questions.why: Speed without quality is failure: under the lifetime labour warranty, rework comes back to us.

questions.q: What widens the gap between estimated and actual hours?
questions.why: A clean, prepared, rework-free job widens the gap.

questions.q: When do you confirm the scope and parts?
questions.why: Confirm the scope and parts the day before so nothing holds the job up.

questions.q: Before you start work, you…
options: Start straight away to save time
Walk the customer through the approved scope and quote, and confirm it's signed
questions.why: Don't start until you've walked the customer through the approved scope and quote and confirmed it's signed.

questions.q: The site doesn't match the scope. You…
options: Call the Install Manager (Charlotte, interim) before starting
Ask the customer what they'd like
questions.why: If the site doesn't match the scope, call the Install Manager before starting.

questions.q: What's the arrival standard?
options: Whenever suits, as long as the work's good
Uniform is optional on small jobs
Drop sheets only on big jobs
On time, in uniform, shoe covers on, drop sheets down
questions.why: On time, in uniform, shoe covers on, drop sheets down, work area protected.

questions.q: What does 7am readiness mean?
options: Rolling to the first job at 7am, fully stocked
questions.why: 7am readiness means rolling to the first job at 7am, fully stocked.

questions.q: Parts pickups should be…
options: Planned, and noted against the job
questions.why: Parts pickups are planned, not mid-job surprises, and every pickup is noted against the job.

questions.q: What's the end-of-day brief for?
options: So anyone can pick the job up tomorrow
questions.why: The end-of-day brief means anyone can pick the job up tomorrow.

questions.q: When are statuses, forms and timesheets updated?
options: At the end of the week
At the end of the month
In real time, as you go
questions.why: Real-time updates, never at the end of the week.

questions.q: What goes in the end-of-day brief?
options: What's done, what's outstanding, and any issues
questions.why: What's done, what's outstanding, and any issues.

questions.q: Which jobs need video and before-and-after photos saved to the job?
questions.why: Videos and before-and-after photos on every job, saved to the job.

questions.q: Before you start, what do you isolate?
questions.why: Isolate water or gas before starting. Every time.

questions.q: Demolition uncovers something that might be asbestos. You…
options: Stop and ask: photograph it, flag it and call the Install Manager or the office
questions.why: Stop and ask if unsure. Never cut, drill or break suspected asbestos.

questions.q: Compliance certificates are…
options: Lodged on time, as part of finishing the job
questions.why: Certificates lodged on time are part of finishing the job.

questions.q: PPE on installs means…
options: Only if the customer is watching
The right PPE for the job, on every job
questions.why: Site safety and the right PPE for the job, on every job.

questions.q: Which hazards are specific to installs?
options: Demolition, wall cavities and roof spaces
questions.why: Install-specific hazards include demolition, wall cavities and roof spaces.

questions.q: When does hot water work peak?
questions.why: Hot water is the biggest install category and peaks June to August.

questions.q: Where do you record a new hot water unit?
questions.why: Record the new unit in ServiceTitan equipment records.

questions.q: When is the manufacturer warranty registered?
questions.why: Register the manufacturer warranty on the day.

questions.q: What do you record for a new unit?
options: The serial, install date and warranty registration
questions.why: Record the serial, install date and warranty registration.

questions.q: Which sign-off is needed for hot water installs?
options: Supervised installs signed off: one electric, one gas or continuous flow
questions.why: A supervised hot water install is signed off: one electric, and one gas or continuous flow.

questions.q: Why follow the standard workflow for each job type?
options: So every install is right first time
questions.why: Standard workflows mean every install is right first time.

questions.q: When do you clean up?
options: Throughout the job, not just at the end
questions.why: Work cleanly throughout, not just at the end.

questions.q: On a renovation, what must you know?
options: Which trade owns what: waterproofing, tiling, electrical
questions.why: On renovations, know which trade owns what.

questions.q: What does a re-pipe need before you start?
options: The customer to choose the pipe
questions.why: Re-pipes need planning: materials and access.

questions.q: Which sign-off is needed for this module?
options: A supervised fixture install plus one other job type
questions.why: A supervised fixture install and one other job type are signed off.

questions.q: What do you test before you leave?
questions.why: Nothing leaves site untested: pressure, flow and leaks.

questions.q: Every return under the lifetime labour warranty is…
options: Unpaid time and a dent in trust
questions.why: Every return under the lifetime labour warranty is unpaid time and a dent in trust.

questions.q: What's your proof of the finished work?
questions.why: The finished-work photos are your proof.

questions.q: The lifetime labour warranty and same-day return mean…
options: Getting it right first time matters even more
questions.why: Because we stand behind the labour for life, getting it right first time matters even more.

questions.q: What do you complete on a live job for sign-off?
questions.why: Complete the testing and commissioning checklist on a live job.

questions.q: You find work that isn't in the approved quote. What's your first step?
questions.why: Stop. Don't carry on with work that isn't in the approved quote.

questions.q: What's the order for a change to scope?
options: Do it, then tell them later
Stop → document → explain and re-price → signed approval → continue
questions.why: Stop → document → explain and re-price → signed approval → continue.

questions.q: Why is unapproved extra work a problem?
options: It breaks the no-hidden-costs promise and is the biggest silent profit leak on installs
questions.why: Unapproved extra work breaks the no-hidden-costs promise and is the biggest silent profit leak on installs.

questions.q: Where does the new price come from?
questions.why: Explain it to the customer and give a new price from the pricebook.

questions.q: You're unsure whether to continue. You…
questions.why: Unsure? Call the Install Manager before you continue.

sim.scenario: Halfway through a bathroom fit-off, you find corroded galvanised pipe that isn't in the scope.

steps.them: Just do it, mate. We'll sort the money out later.
options: "Let me stop and show you what I've found first."
steps.feedback: Stop and photograph it. Never carry on with unapproved work.

steps.them: How much extra are we talking?
options: "I'll price it from the pricebook now and show you exactly."
steps.feedback: Explain it and give a real price from the pricebook, never a guess.

steps.them: Okay, go ahead.
options: Get their signed approval in ServiceTitan, then continue
Add it to the invoice at the end
steps.feedback: Signed approval before you continue keeps the fixed-price promise honest.

questions.q: On every job, you…
questions.why: Look for genuine extra work on every job.

questions.q: You spot extra work. What do you do?
options: Photograph it, explain it, and quote it or raise it
Mention it at the door on the way out
questions.why: Photograph it, explain it, and quote it or raise it.

questions.q: What do you earn on extra work you raise that's sold and completed?
questions.why: That's the 1% for you on extra work you raise that's sold and completed.

questions.q: A problem comes up mid-job. When do you tell the Install Manager?
options: At the end of the day
At the end of the week
questions.why: Tell the Install Manager about problems immediately, not at the end of the day.

questions.q: A job is booked for three days. You…
options: Pace the work so it finishes on time and to standard
questions.why: On a job booked for a set period, pace the work so it finishes on time and to standard.

questions.q: What's the finishing order?
options: Clean, walk-through, warranty, payment and sign-off, review
questions.why: Clean, walk-through, warranty, payment and sign-off, review: in that order, every time.

questions.q: Why show the before-and-after photos?
options: Customers rarely see what was behind the wall
questions.why: Customers rarely see what was behind the wall.

questions.q: How do you explain the warranty?
questions.why: Explain the warranty using the approved wording, so every tech says it the same way.

questions.q: What do you collect before you leave?
options: The balance payment and sign-off in ServiceTitan
questions.why: Collect payment (the balance) and get sign-off in ServiceTitan before leaving.

questions.q: How do you leave the site?
options: Cleaner than you found it, with the rubbish taken away
questions.why: Leave the site cleaner than you found it and take the rubbish away.

questions.q: Why does every tool have a home in the van?
options: Searching for tools is lost time
questions.why: Every tool has a home. Searching for tools is lost time.

questions.q: What happens to unused parts?
options: They stay in the van, just in case
They go back, because parts left in vans are lost profit
questions.why: Unused parts go back. Parts left in vans are lost profit.

questions.q: A tool gets damaged. You…
options: Keep using it until it breaks
questions.why: Report damaged tools straight away.

questions.q: Van stock should be…
options: Topped up when it runs out
Kept up and restocked on time
questions.why: Keep van stock up and restock on time.

questions.q: What does the van audit check?
questions.why: The van passes a stock, returns and tool audit.

questions.q: A job is going to overrun. You…
options: Text at the end of the day
questions.why: Call immediately if a job will overrun.

questions.q: Saturday and emergency cover are…
questions.why: Saturday and emergency cover are part of the role.

questions.q: A return comes back on your own work. You…
options: Fix it promptly and graciously, and learn from it
questions.why: A return on your own work is fixed promptly and graciously, and you learn from it.

questions.q: Something urgent changes on a job. What's the best way to tell dispatch?
questions.why: Urgent changes get a call, not a message.

questions.q: Who dispatches install jobs?
questions.why: Install jobs are dispatched by residential dispatch (Kim).

questions.q: How do most customers first meet Proximity?
questions.why: Most customers meet Proximity through a service call.

questions.q: What makes your average job value rise?
options: Fixing the whole problem and offering genuine options
questions.why: Average job value rises when you fix the whole problem and offer genuine options, not when you push.

questions.q: Every return trip is…
questions.why: Every return trip is lost capacity.

questions.q: What does a Service Tech do at Proximity?
options: Diagnose, fix and sell on the spot
questions.why: Service Techs diagnose, fix and sell on the spot.

questions.q: Which of these is one of your KPIs?
questions.why: First-time fix rate is one of your KPIs, along with average job value, returns and reviews.

questions.q: You've fixed what they called about. Next, you…
options: Check the rest of the system
questions.why: Fix what they called about, then check the rest of the system.

questions.q: What's the diagnostic flow?
options: Listen → inspect → test → root cause → explain
questions.why: Listen → inspect → test → root cause → explain.

questions.q: In the health check, what do you record?
questions.why: The health check feeds reports and future work. Record the 'all good' items too.

questions.q: A finding is borderline. You…
options: Make it sound worse to be safe
Describe it honestly. Never inflate a finding
questions.why: Never inflate a finding. Calm, honest advice builds the reputation.

questions.q: What's the best way to explain a problem?
options: Show photos or footage and explain it in plain English
Use technical terms so you sound expert
questions.why: Show, don't tell: photos and camera footage, explained in plain English.

questions.q: What does every recurring blockage get?
options: A camera inspection, with the footage
questions.why: Every recurring blockage gets a camera inspection, and the footage is what the customer decides on.

questions.q: You clear a drain, but roots or damage are present. The clear is…
options: Temporary. Say so and present all four options
questions.why: A clear is temporary if roots or damage are present. Say so and present all four options.

questions.q: When do blocked drains spike?
questions.why: Blocked drains spike in storm season (summer to autumn).

questions.q: What does the customer base their decision on?
questions.why: The footage is what the customer decides on.

questions.q: Where does the camera footage go?
questions.why: CCTV footage is saved to the job.

sim.scenario: It's the third blockage this year. The customer wants it 'just cleared again, cheaply'.

steps.them: Third time this year. Just clear it again, as cheap as you can.
options: Clear it, then run the camera and show them the footage
steps.feedback: Clear it and show the footage. That's what they'll decide on.

steps.them: Why does it keep happening?
options: Explain what the footage shows, in plain English
steps.feedback: Explain why it keeps happening, using the footage. Calm and honest.

steps.them: So what are my options?
options: All four options, Elite first, and that doing nothing is also a choice
A discount if they sign now
steps.feedback: Present all four, Elite first, without pressure.

questions.q: Why record precise facts, photos and locations on leak jobs?
options: Reports can end up with insurers or in disputes
questions.why: Leak detection reports can end up with insurers or in disputes.

questions.q: A plumbing fault or a waterproofing defect? You…
options: Leave it out of the notes
questions.why: Separate plumbing faults from waterproofing or building defects.

questions.q: When does insurance work spike?
questions.why: Insurance work spikes after storms.

questions.q: Notes for a Leak Detection report contain…
questions.why: Leak Detection reports are findings only. A formal quote follows separately.

questions.q: On a strata leak, what must you record?
questions.why: Strata leaks: record lot vs common property.

questions.q: No hot water is often…
questions.why: No hot water is often urgent, especially with vulnerable occupants.

questions.q: When should you aim to restore hot water?
questions.why: Restore it today if at all possible.

questions.q: An older unit has failed. What do you present?
options: Repair vs replace, across the four options
questions.why: For older units, present repair vs replace across the four options.

questions.q: The customer chooses a replacement. You…
options: Tell them to ring the office
questions.why: Sell the replacement on the spot if they choose it.

questions.q: When is this module refreshed?
options: Every April, before the winter peak
questions.why: Refresh this module every April before the winter peak.

questions.q: When does first-time fix start?
options: The night before: check tomorrow's jobs and stock up
questions.why: First-time fix starts the night before: check tomorrow's jobs and stock up.

questions.q: What does a return trip do?
options: Doubles the cost of the job
questions.why: A return trip doubles the cost of the job.

questions.q: Replacing a part, you…
options: Replace like-for-like, or offer an upgrade from the pricebook
questions.why: Replace like-for-like, or offer an upgrade from the pricebook.

questions.q: You don't have the part on board. What's the aim?
options: Book a return next week by default
Find an option that avoids a return trip
questions.why: No part on board: find a way to avoid a return trip.

questions.q: What wins first-time fix?
questions.why: First-time fix comes from preparation and van stock.

questions.q: A job has more than one sensible fix. You present…
options: All four options, Elite first, and the customer chooses
questions.why: Every job with more than one sensible fix gets all four options, Elite first.

questions.q: Bundle discounts are…
options: Never given: every line comes from the pricebook
questions.why: Never discount a bundle: every line comes from the pricebook.

questions.q: The customer chooses work that can be done today. You…
questions.why: If they choose work that's done today, you finish it today.

questions.q: How is bigger work booked?
options: With a 50% deposit and a proper handover
questions.why: Bigger work is booked with a 50% deposit and a proper handover.

questions.q: What do you offer on every completed job?
questions.why: Offer the Care Plan on every completed job.

sim.scenario: The customer wants the cheapest fix only and is wary of being sold anything.

steps.them: Just fix the leak. I don't want to be sold anything.
options: "Sure, but you really need a whole new system."
"I'll do it cheaper if you add more."
steps.feedback: Respect it and fix what they asked for.

steps.them: Done? Anything else I should know?
options: Briefly show the photos of what you found and what each one means
Hand them a long priced list
steps.feedback: Briefly show what you found. No pressure.

steps.them: Hmm. What would sorting that out cost?
options: Present the options, Elite first, and let them decide
steps.feedback: Present the options and let them decide, with no pressure.

questions.q: Who are our most loyal customers?
questions.why: Members are our most loyal customers.

questions.q: A preventive visit should feel…
questions.why: Preventive visits are reassuring first.

questions.q: When do you offer the Care Plan?
questions.why: Offer the Care Plan on every completed job.

questions.q: Offering the Care Plan is…
options: One of the weekly tracked habits
questions.why: Offering the Care Plan is one of the weekly tracked habits.

questions.q: A preventive visit finds everything in good shape. That's…
options: A good result. Say so clearly
questions.why: Preventive visits are reassuring first. 'Everything's in good shape' is a good result.

questions.q: What's the first thing you do at an emergency?
questions.why: Make safe first: isolate, contain, protect.

questions.q: Emergency customers…
options: Remember how they were treated for life
questions.why: Emergency customers remember how they were treated for life.

questions.q: Once it's safe, you…
options: Present the four options for the permanent fix
questions.why: Make safe first, then present the four options for the permanent fix.

questions.q: When do the highest-intent calls come in?
questions.why: 6pm to 10pm and weekends are when the highest-intent calls come in.

questions.q: Which of these is an emergency?
options: An active leak coming through a ceiling
questions.why: An active leak is an emergency. Make it safe fast.

sim.scenario: Water is coming through the kitchen ceiling. The customer is panicking and angry about after-hours rates.

steps.them: Water's pouring through the ceiling! Do something!
options: Take photos for the report first
steps.feedback: Isolate immediately. Make safe first.

steps.them: And what's this going to cost me at this hour?!
options: "I know this is stressful. Here's how the after-hours rate works…"
steps.feedback: Acknowledge the stress and explain the rate calmly.

steps.them: Okay. Now what?
options: Make it safe, then give the options for the permanent fix
Start the biggest repair straight away
Tell them to ring someone tomorrow
steps.feedback: Make safe, then give the options.

questions.q: The fix costs more than the property manager's approval limit. You…
options: Get written approval before going over
questions.why: Never exceed the PM's approval limit without written approval.

questions.q: On a tenant job, who decides?
options: The property manager, not the tenant
questions.why: Tenants aren't the decision-maker.

questions.q: Who does larger strata work go to?
questions.why: Larger strata work goes to Bella.

questions.q: Who does commercial work go to?
questions.why: Commercial work goes to Alex.

questions.q: With a landlord, the focus is…
questions.why: Landlords: protecting the asset.

sim.scenario: The hot water has failed. The PM's approval limit is $300 and the fix costs more.

steps.them: Can you just fix it? The agent won't mind.
options: Fix it all and bill the agent
Make it safe and explain the agent has to approve anything over their limit
steps.feedback: Make safe and explain to the tenant. The agent approves.

steps.them: So what happens now?
options: Wait for the agent to ring you
Do the cheapest thing under $300, even if it won't fix it
Send the PM photos and the options
steps.feedback: Send the PM photos and options so they can decide quickly.

steps.them: (The PM replies) Okay, go ahead with Standard.
steps.feedback: Document the approval before you proceed.

questions.q: Why is prejudging the most expensive objection?
options: Because we raise it for the customer
questions.why: Prejudging is the most expensive objection, because we raise it for the customer.

questions.q: Every quote has…
options: At least one bundled tier, built from findings
questions.why: Every quote has at least one bundled tier, built from findings, never from a script.

questions.q: How is a bundle priced?
options: Every line from the pricebook, with no bundle discount
questions.why: No bundle discounts, ever. Every line is priced from the pricebook.

questions.q: You've quoted the same bundle twice. It should…
options: Become a template, reviewed and signed off
questions.why: If you've quoted the same bundle twice, it should be a template.

questions.q: A modest house and a quiet owner. You…
options: Present every option, Elite first: their choice reveals the budget
Ask what they can afford first
questions.why: Never prejudge. Present every option, every time. Their choice reveals the budget.

sim.scenario: A tidy older home and a quiet, careful owner. The 14-year-old unit has failed, there's no tempering valve, the flexis are perished and the mains pressure is high.

steps.them: Just the hot water, mate.
options: "Happy to. Can I quickly show you a few things I found while I was here?"
steps.feedback: Don't prejudge, and don't skip the findings.

steps.them: Why does all that matter?
options: Explain it as one ageing system failing in stages, using the photos
Read out a list of separate jobs
steps.feedback: Frame it as one problem, not a list of jobs.

steps.them: What are the options, then?
options: All four, Elite first (Essential is the unit only; Elite is the full bundle with a Care Plan), and let them choose
steps.feedback: All four, Elite first, and let them choose.

questions.q: Technicians who talk too much…
options: Miss the details that justify the bigger option
questions.why: Ask, then listen. Technicians who talk too much miss the details that justify the bigger option.

questions.q: What do customers really buy?
questions.why: Customers buy peace of mind, not parts.

questions.q: Describing what happens if they leave it should be…
options: Calm, honest consequences, not scare tactics
questions.why: Consequences, not scare tactics: describe what really happens, calmly and honestly.

questions.q: What does the up-front agreement do?
options: Makes 'not yet' a normal outcome, which takes pressure off both sides
questions.why: The up-front agreement makes 'not yet' a normal outcome.

questions.q: Which of these is a trust signal?
options: They start asking 'when can you start?'
questions.why: Forward questions like 'how long will it last?' and 'when can you start?' are the trust shift.

sim.scenario: They say all the right things but only ask defensive questions. You're tempted to present now.

steps.them: Right. So how much is all this going to be?
options: "I'll get to that. Can I ask how long you're planning to stay in the house?"
steps.feedback: Hold off presenting. Ask discovery questions first.

steps.them: We've had nothing but trouble with the water pressure since we moved in.
options: "What has that meant for you, day to day?"
steps.feedback: Ask how the problem affects them. Diagnose the person, not just the pipes.

steps.them: How long would the proper fix last? When could you start?
options: That's the trust shift: present now, Elite first
Leave a quote in the letterbox
steps.feedback: Present once they start asking forward questions.

questions.q: Why lead with Elite?
options: The first number sets the scale, so everything below sounds reasonable
questions.why: The first number they hear sets the scale.

questions.q: Lead with Essential and…
options: Everything above sounds like a rip-off
questions.why: Lead with Essential and everything above sounds like a rip-off.

questions.q: You've just said a $30K price. You…
questions.why: Scope. Price. Silence. Let them speak first.

questions.q: What do most techs do wrong with big numbers?
options: Discount before the customer has even objected
questions.why: Most techs discount before the customer has even objected. Don't.

questions.q: How do you get comfortable saying a big number?
options: Practise it out loud until it's boring
questions.why: Say a $30K number out loud without flinching. Practise it until it's boring.

sim.scenario: A 1960s home with galvanised pipe, three leaks this year and low pressure. A couple: one is keen, the other thinks 'just patch the leaks'.

steps.them: Can't you just patch the leaks?
options: Walk through what failure looks like (the burst, the ceiling, the damage), calmly and honestly
steps.feedback: Anchor honestly: show what failure looks like before the price.

steps.them: So what are you suggesting?
options: Present Elite first, then narrow to the two that fit this home
Start with patching, then mention the re-pipe
steps.feedback: Elite first, then narrow to two. Don't read it like a menu.

steps.them: And the full re-pipe is how much?
steps.feedback: State the price and hold the silence.

questions.q: When is finance mentioned?
options: Three times: during the inspection, with the options, and after the price
questions.why: Seed it three times: during the inspection, while walking through options, and after the price and the silence.

questions.q: What's the financed benchmark?
questions.why: If fewer than 40% of big jobs are financed, it isn't being offered consistently.

questions.q: Finance is…
options: The 'how', not the 'what': lead with the solution
questions.why: Lead with the solution; finance removes the barrier.

questions.q: Who do you offer finance to?
options: Only people who look like they need it
Every customer on every big job, with the same line and tone
questions.why: Same line, same tone, to every customer on every big job.

questions.q: Where does finance appear on the proposal?
options: Nowhere: HomePro sits outside ServiceTitan, and the proposal shows the full scope and real price
questions.why: HomePro sits outside ServiceTitan, so the proposal never mentions finance.

sim.scenario: You've stated $14,800 for the Premium option. They go silent and look at each other.

steps.them: (Silence.)
options: Fill the silence by justifying the price
steps.feedback: Hold the silence. It feels long to you, not to them.

steps.them: That's… a lot in one hit.
options: "Like I mentioned, I can turn that into a weekly figure in about two minutes."
steps.feedback: Bring finance home as something they've already heard.

steps.them: What would it be weekly?
steps.feedback: Always use HomePro's real numbers, never a guess.

questions.q: 'I can't afford it' usually means…
options: They don't see the value yet, they're scared of the number, or nobody gave them a way to say yes
questions.why: 'I can't afford it' almost never means they can't pay.

questions.q: How do you separate can't from won't?
options: "Totally fair. Can I ask what feels like too much about it?"
questions.why: Stay calm and curious, then let them talk.

questions.q: When does the price come down?
options: At the end of the month
questions.why: Price only comes down when scope comes out. Otherwise they learn our first number was fake.

questions.q: "Can you sharpen your pencil?" You…
options: "Let me see what the office can do."
Step down an option: you can't discount
questions.why: You can't discount. Never say 'let me see what the office can do'. Step down an option instead.

questions.q: A respectful 'not yet' with a booked follow-up is…
questions.why: A respectful 'not yet' with a booked follow-up is a win, not a loss.

sim.scenario: Three customers, three objections. Use the lines from the session.

steps.them: Door 1: you say the price and they go silent.
options: Hold the silence and let them speak first
Ask if they want a cheaper one
steps.feedback: The silence feels long to you, not to them.

steps.them: Door 2: "Can you do it cheaper?" on the Premium option.
options: "Let me see what the office can do."
"I can't do that price on the full job. If we do just the urgent part today, here's where we land."
steps.feedback: Never discount for free. If the price comes down, scope comes out.

steps.them: Door 3: "Money's tight right now. We'll have to think about it."
options: "Totally fair. Can I ask what feels like too much about it?"
steps.feedback: Separate can't from won't, then remove the barrier.

questions.q: What do commercial buyers want?
questions.why: Commercial buyers want reliability, compliance and response time.

questions.q: A commercial quote has to work for…
options: People who weren't in the room
questions.why: The quote has to work for people who weren't in the room.

questions.q: Every open estimate has…
options: A next action and a date in ServiceTitan
questions.why: Every open estimate has a next action and a date in ServiceTitan.

questions.q: Unsold quotes are followed up within…
questions.why: Follow-up within 48 hours is one of the weekly habits.

questions.q: On commercial and strata work, who owns the relationship?
options: Alex (commercial) and Bella (strata). You own the scope and the quote
questions.why: Alex and Bella own the relationship. You own the scope and the quote.

sim.scenario: Three quotes for a building-wide hot water and riser problem. Ours is the most expensive, and the committee meets next week.

steps.them: We've got three quotes and yours is the most expensive.
options: "Happy to help. What does the committee need to decide, and by when?"
steps.feedback: Agree up front what the committee needs to decide.

steps.them: So why are you dearer?
options: Compare scope like-for-like: show what the other quotes leave out
steps.feedback: A cheaper quote almost always has a smaller scope. Show the gaps.

steps.them: It's a lot for the committee to approve in one go.
options: Offer a staged works program, and offer to attend the committee meeting
steps.feedback: Stage it and offer to attend the meeting.
